correctness.rationale: A two-dimensional Gamma hypercube has four vertices and each radius-one hyperedge is a three-vertex subset. A singular square mapped to a simple graph edge-hypergraph can use at most two target vertices, or else three distinct images would occupy some three-source hyperedge. Every nondegenerate 2-square therefore has image exactly a unique graph edge. Both C2 and normalized C1 split as direct sums by that target edge, and d2 preserves each summand. For any edge target {a,b}, every gamma cube into it is singular, so the normalized prism Pk(f)=(f on final coordinate 0, constant a on final coordinate 1) gives dP2-P1d=-id, filling all edge-supported 2-cycles integrally. Finite sums yield H2Gamma(G;Z)=0, and same integral contraction works over any abelian group. No assertion for higher k where edge-localization can fail or for conventional Box cubical homology. Independently checked the signed prism identity on all ten nondegenerate binary squares and verified the normalization/2-color property.

originality.rationale: Zaidi and Jamil (2026) introduced Gamma cubical homology and compared low degrees, including H0/H1 and excision behavior; their accessible full text was inspected across definitions, examples, and section 5, with no identified all-graph H2 vanishing theorem. Ordinary Box graph cubical H2 can be nonzero and cannot cover the Gamma statement without an isomorphism theorem, contradicted by the three homology theories being distinct. The direct edgewise contraction is a new proposed structural boundary, though equivalent unpublished work is possible.
residual_risks: Potentially the foundational 2026 preprint has an implicit chain-contraction corollary not expressly named; inspected definitions/theorems do not provide a universal graph statement outright.
No claim that H3Gamma vanishes or that graph Box homology has the same result; the theories differ.
